Occurrences.Kwic: 其僧往沙彌處問：「適來和尚打爾作什麼？」沙彌云：「若不是我，和尚不打某甲。」師云：「者僧克由叵耐，將一杓屎潑他二員古佛。諸上座若能辯得，非唯趙睦二州雪屈，亦乃翠峯與天下老宿無過。」

Senses.Explanation: `克由叵耐` is an opaque colloquial outburst expressing exasperation or sharp disapproval. Yushan Shangsi inserts it while denouncing old worthies for fouling the teaching seat. Xuedou Chongxian applies it to the monk whose explanation smeared Zhaozhou and Muzhou; these rebuking frames establish force without recovering a graph-by-graph etymology.

Senses.Note: The phrase is an encounter verdict in this case, not a neutral measure of physical endurance.

Senses.Explanation: Muzhou greets a newly arrived visitor with the abrupt verdict “especially intolerable,” leaving the visitor unable to fathom it before driving the whole group out. In Muzhou Daoming’s record, a new arrival comes to call. Senses.Explanation: This stock appraisal pictures redundant commerce: trying to sell all of Yangzhou while already inside one’s own house. Chan records apply the scene in encounters and verses. Its uses retain the impossible redundancy of selling a whole place from inside one’s own house; local cases decide whom the appraisal addresses. The cited passages span 5 works and preserve the exact headword in the quoted Chinese. The gloss reports the shared use and leaves each surrounding case to its own recorded exchange.

Senses.Note: One controlling Tier-2 complete exchange; later case copies and lamps are excluded.

Senses.Explanation: To provide a meal for the monastic assembly is a public sponsorship event that frequently occasions a hall address. Dahui Zonggao speaks within one such continuing discourse. Other records name donors or occasions while the invited master delivers the address; sponsorship and utterance are kept separate. The phrase therefore names the meal-giving event, not the speaker of every discourse that follows it.
